7.1.crux: Deforestation means cutting down forests and using the land for other things, mostly farming, homes, factories, furniture and fuel.

cards.title: What is deforestation?

steps.text: A thick forest
Trees are cut down
The land is used for farms, houses or factories

say: Clearing forests and using the land for other purposes is called deforestation.

cards.title: Why forests are cleared
say: Most deforestation is caused by people.
Fires and droughts can also destroy forests.

cards.title: What forests give us
say: When a forest is cut down, we lose all of these together.

crux_points: Deforestation is clearing forests to use the land for other purposes.
People clear forests for farms, homes, factories, furniture and fuel.
Forest fires and droughts are natural causes.

quiz.q: Which is a natural cause of deforestation?
quiz.why: Forest fires and severe droughts are natural causes; the rest are caused by people.

quiz.q: Deforestation means…
options: Clearing forests and using the land for other purposes
quiz.why: That is the meaning of deforestation.

7.2.crux: Without forests we get less rain, more heat, more floods and droughts, soil washes away, and fertile land can turn into desert.

cards.title: What happens when trees go

items.sub: Fewer trees to take it in
Rain runs off instead of soaking in
No roots to hold back the water

say: Trees control water, temperature and the gases in the air.
Removing them upsets the balance of nature.

cards.title: From forest to desert

steps.text: Tree roots hold the soil together
Trees are cut down
Wind and water carry away the top fertile soil (soil erosion)
The land slowly becomes a desert (desertification)

say: The top layer of soil holds humus and nutrients.
Once it's gone, plants can't grow well.

cards.title: Forests and rain

steps.text: Trees take up water from the soil.
They release water vapour into the air.
The vapour helps form clouds.
Rain falls back on the land and forest.

say: Fewer trees means less water goes back into the air, so less rain falls.

crux_points: Deforestation raises temperature, pollution and carbon dioxide.
It reduces rainfall and groundwater and causes floods and droughts.
Soil erosion can turn fertile land into desert (desertification).

quiz.q: When fertile land slowly turns into desert, it is called…
quiz.why: Desertification follows soil erosion after trees are removed.

quiz.q: Why do floods increase after deforestation?
options: No roots hold back the water
quiz.why: Tree roots and forest soil soak up rain; without them water rushes off the land.

7.3.crux: To save plants and animals, special protected areas are set aside: wildlife sanctuaries, national parks and biosphere reserves.

cards.title: Biodiversity
say: Biodiversity is the variety of living things in an area: plants, animals and microbes.
Each depends on the others.

cards.title: Protected areas

items.name: Wildlife sanctuary
items.eg: Animals protected from hunting and capture

items.name: Biosphere reserve
items.eg: Large area protecting plants, animals and tribal ways of life

say: Rules stop people from cutting trees, hunting or grazing inside these areas.
cards.remember: Sanctuary, national park, biosphere reserve: three kinds of protected area.

cards.title: How you can help

items.text: Never buy products made from wild animals

say: Conservation is everyone's job, not just the forest department's.

crux_points: Biodiversity is the variety of living things in an area.
Protected areas conserve forests and wildlife.
The three main kinds are wildlife sanctuaries, national parks and biosphere reserves.

quiz.q: Biodiversity means…
options: The variety of living things in an area
Only the trees in a forest
quiz.why: Biodiversity covers all the plants, animals and microbes in an area.

quiz.q: Which is a protected area?
quiz.why: National parks, sanctuaries and biosphere reserves are protected areas.

7.4.crux: A biosphere reserve is a large protected area that conserves its plants, animals and microbes, and the traditional life of the people living there.

cards.title: Inside a biosphere reserve
say: The biosphere is the part of Earth where living things exist.
A biosphere reserve protects the variety of life in a large area, along with the culture of local people.

cards.title: Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve
say: A biosphere reserve can contain other protected areas inside it.
Pachmarhi contains one national park and two wildlife sanctuaries.

cards.title: Everything is connected

steps.text: Grass and plants make food from sunlight
Deer eat the plants
Tigers eat the deer

say: If one living thing disappears, others that depend on it suffer too.
That's why a reserve protects all the life in an area, not just one animal.

crux_points: A biosphere reserve is a large area that conserves biodiversity.
It also protects the traditional life of local tribal people.
It can contain national parks and sanctuaries, like Pachmarhi.

quiz.q: Which part of a biosphere reserve is most strictly protected?
quiz.why: The core area is left undisturbed for wildlife.

quiz.q: Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve contains…
options: Satpura National Park and two sanctuaries
quiz.why: It includes Satpura National Park and the Bori and Pachmarhi sanctuaries.

7.5.crux: Flora means all the plants of an area and fauna means all its animals.

cards.title: Flora and fauna
say: These are some of the plants and animals of the Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve.

cards.title: Flora and fauna depend on each other

items.text: Plants give animals food and shelter
Animals carry pollen and spread seeds

say: The plants and animals of a forest help each other survive.

cards.title: Your own area
say: Every place has its own flora and fauna.
cards.think: Name three plants and three animals that live near your school.

crux_points: Flora: the plants of a particular area.
Fauna: the animals of a particular area.
Every area has its own flora and fauna.

quiz.q: Teak and sal trees are part of the area's…
quiz.why: Flora means the plants of an area.

quiz.q: Which of these is fauna?
quiz.why: Fauna means the animals of an area.

7.6.crux: Endemic species are plants or animals found naturally only in one particular area and nowhere else.

cards.title: Found only here
say: An endemic species lives naturally only in a particular region.

cards.title: Why they're at risk
say: If an endemic species loses its home, it has nowhere else to go.
cards.remember: Endemic = found only in one place; lose that place, lose the species.

cards.title: What is a species?
say: A species is a group of living things that can breed with each other.
Members of one species have common features.

crux_points: Endemic species are found naturally only in one area.
The Indian giant squirrel is endemic to Pachmarhi.
Habitat loss, population growth and new species threaten them.

quiz.q: An endemic species is one that…
options: Is found naturally only in a particular area
quiz.why: Endemic species are not found naturally anywhere else.

quiz.q: Which animal is endemic to the Pachmarhi area?
quiz.why: The Indian giant squirrel is endemic to that region.

7.7.crux: A wildlife sanctuary is a place where wild animals are protected; hunting (poaching) and capturing them are strictly banned.

cards.title: A safe home for animals

steps.text: Animals live in their natural surroundings
Killing (poaching) or capturing animals is strictly banned
Local people may graze cattle or collect firewood in some areas

say: In a sanctuary, animals are protected from disturbance.

cards.title: Threats to sanctuaries

items.sub: Illegal killing for skins, tusks, horns

say: Despite the rules, poaching still happens and must be stopped.
cards.remember: Poaching = illegal killing or capturing of wild animals.

cards.title: Sanctuary or zoo?

cols.head: Wildlife sanctuary
cells: Animals live in their natural habitat

cols.head: Zoo
cells: Made to look like their habitat

say: Zoos also protect animals, but in an artificial setting.

crux_points: A wildlife sanctuary protects animals in their natural home.
Poaching and capturing animals are strictly prohibited.
Some limited activities by local people are allowed.

quiz.q: Illegal killing of wild animals is called…
quiz.why: Poaching is the illegal hunting or capturing of wild animals.

quiz.q: How is a sanctuary different from a zoo?
options: Animals live in their natural habitat
quiz.why: A sanctuary protects animals in their natural surroundings.

7.8.crux: A national park is a large area that protects a whole ecosystem; Satpura National Park in Madhya Pradesh is famous for its tigers and teak.

cards.title: A national park protects everything
say: Animals in a national park can freely use their habitat and natural resources.
The whole ecosystem is protected.

cards.title: Satpura National Park
say: Satpura National Park is in the Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve.
Its rock shelters show how people lived in the forest long ago.

cards.title: Project Tiger

steps.text: Tiger numbers were falling fast
In 1973 the government launched Project Tiger
Tiger reserves now protect tigers and their homes

say: Tigers are one of the many species at risk of dying out in India.

crux_points: A national park protects a whole ecosystem: plants, animals and landscape.
Satpura National Park has tigers, fine teak and ancient rock paintings.
Project Tiger (1973) protects tigers in tiger reserves.

quiz.q: When was Project Tiger launched?
quiz.why: Project Tiger was launched in 1973 to protect tigers.

quiz.q: Satpura National Park is famous for…
quiz.why: It has tigers, the finest Indian teak and prehistoric rock shelters.

7.9.crux: The Red Data Book keeps a record of all plants and animals that are endangered, to help protect them.

cards.title: From safe to extinct
say: Endangered animals are those whose numbers have fallen so low they might die out.
Extinct species no longer exist anywhere, like the dinosaurs.

cards.title: The Red Data Book

steps.text: A source book that records endangered species
Kept by an international organisation
India also keeps its own Red Data Book for its plants and animals

say: Knowing which species are in danger helps us take steps to save them.
cards.remember: Red Data Book = the record of endangered species.

cards.title: Why species become endangered
say: Most species become endangered because of human activities.

crux_points: Endangered species are at risk of dying out.
Extinct species no longer exist.
The Red Data Book records endangered plants and animals.

quiz.q: What does the Red Data Book record?
quiz.why: It is the source book of all endangered animals and plants.

quiz.q: A species that no longer exists anywhere is…
quiz.why: Extinct species, like dinosaurs, are gone forever.

7.10.crux: Migration is when animals travel far from their home at the same time every year, often to escape cold and to breed.

cards.title: Why birds migrate

steps.text: Their home becomes very cold in winter
Birds fly thousands of kilometres to warmer places
They lay eggs and raise young there
When the weather changes, they fly back home

say: Migratory birds travel at a particular time every year because of changes in climate.

cards.title: Visitors to India

items.sub: Visit Indian lakes and wetlands in winter

say: Protecting wetlands keeps these visitors safe.
cards.remember: Migration: moving to another habitat for part of every year.

cards.title: Helping migrating birds
say: Birds that travel thousands of kilometres need safe places to stop.

crux_points: Migration is moving from one habitat to another for part of every year.
Birds migrate to escape harsh cold and to breed.
Siberian cranes migrate to India in winter.

quiz.q: Why do Siberian cranes come to India?
quiz.why: They migrate to escape the very cold weather and to breed.

quiz.q: Migration happens…
options: At a particular time every year
quiz.why: Migratory animals move at the same season every year.

7.11.crux: Making paper uses lots of trees, so saving, reusing and recycling paper helps save forests.

cards.title: Trees into paper
say: It takes about 17 full-grown trees to make one tonne of paper.

cards.title: Recycle, recycle, recycle

steps.text: We use paper for notebooks and printing.
Used paper is collected separately.
It is pulped and made into new paper.
New paper is used again.

say: Paper can be recycled five to seven times.
If each student saves one sheet a day, we can save many trees a year.
cards.remember: Save, reuse and recycle paper to save trees.

cards.title: Easy ways to save paper
say: Recycling also saves water and energy used to make new paper.

crux_points: Making 1 tonne of paper uses about 17 full-grown trees.
Paper can be recycled 5 to 7 times.
Saving and recycling paper saves trees.

quiz.q: About how many full-grown trees are needed to make 1 tonne of paper?
quiz.why: About 17 full-grown trees make one tonne of paper.

quiz.q: How many times can paper be recycled?
quiz.why: Paper fibres get shorter each time, so it can be recycled about 5 to 7 times.

7.12.crux: Reforestation means planting new trees where forests were destroyed, ideally of the same kinds that grew there before.

cards.title: Bringing forests back

steps.text: A forest area has been cut
New trees of the same types are planted
Over years, the forest grows back

say: Restocking a destroyed forest by planting new trees is called reforestation.
We should plant at least as many trees as we cut.

cards.title: Nature can do it too
say: If a cleared area is left alone, the forest may grow back naturally.

cards.title: The law helps

items.sub: Meets the needs of those living in and near forests

say: India has laws to protect forests and the people who depend on them.
cards.remember: Plant trees, protect forests, follow the law.

crux_points: Reforestation is planting new trees in place of destroyed forests.
Forests can also regrow naturally if left undisturbed.
India's Forest (Conservation) Act protects natural forests.

quiz.q: Planting new trees in a destroyed forest is called…
quiz.why: Reforestation restocks a forest with new trees.

quiz.q: Which trees are best for reforesting an area?
options: The same types that grew there before
quiz.why: Planting the original types restores the natural forest.
